name: Outlook Home Page
description:
Adversaries may abuse Microsoft Outlook's Home Page feature to obtain persistence on a compromised system. Outlook Home Page is a legacy feature used to customize the presentation of Outlook folders. This feature allows for an internal or external URL to be loaded and presented whenever a folder is opened. A malicious HTML page can be crafted that will execute code when loaded by Outlook Home Page.(Citation: SensePost Outlook Home Page)

Once malicious home pages have been added to the user’s mailbox, they will be loaded when Outlook is started. Malicious Home Pages will execute when the right Outlook folder is loaded/reloaded.(Citation: SensePost Outlook Home Page)

references.description: Fox, C., Vangel, D. (2018, April 22). Detect and Remediate Outlook Rules and Custom Forms Injections Attacks in Office 365. Retrieved February 4, 2019.
SensePost. (2017, September 21). NotRuler - The opposite of Ruler, provides blue teams with the ability to detect Ruler usage against Exchange. Retrieved February 4, 2019.
Stalmans, E. (2017, October 11). Outlook Home Page – Another Ruler Vector. Retrieved February 4, 2019.

telemetry.name: Application Log Content
telemetry.description: Application-emitted audit or operational event content.
telemetry.collection_focus: Select the application event family required by the detection and document its native schema before normalization.

providers.name: Application audit logs
providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

telemetry.name: Command Execution
telemetry.description: Execution of a command and its interpreter or parent context.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect process command lines and relevant shell/interpreter audit; shell history alone is neither complete nor tamper-resistant.

providers.name: PowerShell Script Block Logging
providers.scope: Script content via event 4104 when configured; channel depends on PowerShell edition.

providers.name: Sysmon process events
providers.scope: Interpreter launch and parent context, not full script content.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: execve-family execution context; shell built-ins need additional instrumentation.

configuration: Enable Script Block Logging through the policy/configuration for the installed edition. Forward Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational for Windows PowerShell, or PowerShellCore/Operational for PowerShell 7.
Retain script-block ID and fragment ordering alongside process creation. Protect access to collected script text; secrets may be included.
On Linux, use narrowly scoped Audit execution rules for the lab account and supported architectures, and retain joined SYSCALL/EXECVE/PATH records.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Script content and process command lines are different signals. Logging may be partial, fragmented, filtered or disabled; never assume a command line reveals everything executed.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per host role and principal: rare interpreters, command argument patterns and parent-child sequences. Normalize scripts carefully; obfuscation, administrative automation and missing command lines change visibility.

telemetry.name: Module Load
telemetry.description: A module or library being loaded into a running process.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope Sysmon ImageLoad (7) to lab processes/paths; retain module hash, signer and destination process. Inventory alone does not prove a module loaded.

providers.scope: Windows event-based collection; enable the event types needed below.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: Linux alternative for supported system-call and file events; different semantics and fields.

providers.name: Apple Endpoint Security clients
providers.scope: macOS alternative where the subscribed event exists; requires an entitled, approved client, not an iOS collector.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.

strategies.name: Detect Persistence via Outlook Home Page Exploitation

analytics.name: Analytic 0502
analytics.guidance: Adversary uses a tool like Ruler to configure a malicious Outlook folder Home Page that loads a remote or embedded HTML payload upon folder interaction. Execution chain begins with Outlook launching, a specific folder being accessed, and a suspicious child process being spawned or COM-based execution invoked.

tuning.description: Home Page can be configured on any folder like Calendar, Inbox, or custom folders
The Home Page URL may point to internal or external content, hosted on trusted or unknown domains
Execution may result in launch of scripting hosts (e.g., mshta.exe, wscript.exe) from outlook.exe
Execution may occur only when the specific folder is accessed after launch, not immediately at startup
Behavior may vary if the folder's form view is customized or suppressed via GPO

log_sources.name: WinEventLog:Application
log_sources.channel: Outlook logs indicating failure to load or render HTML page in Home Page view

log_sources.name: WinEventLog:PowerShell
log_sources.channel: Execution of PowerShell script to enumerate or remove malicious Home Page folder config

analytics.name: Analytic 0503
analytics.guidance: Malicious HTML or script is rendered as a Home Page for a specific Outlook folder. Outlook accesses that folder, loads remote content, and executes embedded JavaScript or ActiveX/COM logic resulting in unauthorized actions or local execution.

tuning.description: Home Page customization may not be audited unless detailed message or folder auditing is enabled
Anomalous access to folders not usually interacted with can signal triggering of malicious view
Mail clients may restrict remote Home Page content unless domain is explicitly allowed

log_sources.name: m365:unified
log_sources.channel: Folder configuration updated with external or HTML-formatted Home Page via Set-MailboxFolder

log_sources.name: m365:messagetrace
log_sources.channel: Inbound email triggering Outlook to auto-access folder tied to malicious Home Page

software.name: Ruler
software.description: [Ruler](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0358) can be used to automate the abuse of Outlook Home Pages to establish persistence.(Citation: SensePost Ruler GitHub)

references.description: SensePost. (2016, August 18). Ruler: A tool to abuse Exchange services. Retrieved February 4, 2019.

actors.name: OilRig
actors.description: [OilRig](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0049) has abused the Outlook Home Page feature for persistence. [OilRig](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0049) has also used CVE-2017-11774 to roll back the initial patch designed to protect against Home Page abuse.(Citation: FireEye Outlook Dec 2019)

references.description: McWhirt, M., Carr, N., Bienstock, D. (2019, December 4). Breaking the Rules: A Tough Outlook for Home Page Attacks (CVE-2017-11774). Retrieved June 23, 2020.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.description: On Windows 10, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to prevent Office applications from creating child processes and from writing potentially malicious executable content to disk. (Citation: win10_asr)

references.description: Microsoft. (2021, July 2). Use attack surface reduction rules to prevent malware infection. Retrieved June 24, 2021.

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.description: For the Outlook methods, blocking macros may be ineffective as the Visual Basic engine used for these features is separate from the macro scripting engine.(Citation: SensePost Outlook Forms) Microsoft has released patches to try to address each issue. Ensure KB3191938 which blocks Outlook Visual Basic and displays a malicious code warning, KB4011091 which disables custom forms by default, and KB4011162 which removes the legacy Home Page feature, are applied to systems.(Citation: SensePost Outlook Home Page)

references.description: Stalmans, E. (2017, April 28). Outlook Forms and Shells. Retrieved February 4, 2019.
Stalmans, E. (2017, October 11). Outlook Home Page – Another Ruler Vector. Retrieved February 4, 2019.

candidates.name: Install Outlook Home Page Persistence
candidates.description:
This test simulates persistence being added to a host via the Outlook Home Page functionality. This causes Outlook to retrieve URL containing a malicious payload every time the targeted folder is viewed.

Triggering the payload requires manually opening Outlook and viewing the targetted folder (e.g. Inbox).

url.description: URL to Outlook Home Page containing the payload to execute (can be local file:// or remote https://)

outlook_version.description: Version of Outlook that is installed

outlook_folder.description: Name of the Outlook folder to modify the homepage setting for

simulation.prerequisites: Use disposable lab hosts and test accounts, explicit target allowlists, a clean snapshot, bounded egress and a restore plan. Review every candidate and dependency before any execution.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
